# Expose per-project Kueue quota data for admin consumption reporting

## Description

This epic delivers the Distributed Workloads side of administrator chargeback
reporting: the per-project Kueue quota information that the Dashboard admin
view needs to display current-month GPU consumption against each project's
quota. Kueue is the platform's queueing system with the ClusterQueue /
LocalQueue quota model; this epic makes per-project quota attribution available
for consumption by the reporting UI. This is Tier 1 work — it is independent of
the in-flight GPU usage metering strategy and can start immediately.

## Scope

- Make each project's Kueue quota (as applicable to GPU resources) available
  for retrieval in a form the Dashboard admin view can consume.
- Ensure the quota information covers the projects that participate in shared
  GPU clusters.
- Coordinate with the Dashboard team on the shape of the quota data consumed by
  the admin view (attribution of queues to projects).
- No metering/collection work — per-project GPU-hour usage data is delivered by
  the separate metering strategy and is out of scope here.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Per-project Kueue quota information is retrievable by the Dashboard admin
  view for GPU-related quotas.
- Quota attribution covers all projects with Kueue quotas on shared GPU
  clusters.
- The Dashboard team confirms the exposed quota data is sufficient to render
  the current-month consumption-vs-quota comparison.
- Existing Kueue queueing behavior is unaffected (no regression to admission or
  scheduling).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): Dashboard admin view shows current-month consumption against
  each project's Kueue quota — this epic provides the quota dimension.

# Dashboard GPU-hour chargeback reporting service with stable API and CSV export

## Description

This epic delivers the reporting capability that computes per-project GPU-hour
consumption reports over selectable time ranges from the metering data
delivered by the in-flight GPU usage metering strategy, and exposes those
reports through a stable API suitable for finance tooling, including CSV
export. It provides the data layer that the administrator-facing console view
builds on. Reports are denominated in GPU-hours; currency/cost-rate modelling
is out of scope.

## Scope

- Compute per-project GPU-hour consumption reports over selectable time ranges
  from the metering data (consumed, not re-implemented — no collection
  pipeline work).
- Expose report retrieval through a stable API that finance tooling can
  integrate against.
- Provide CSV export of reports.
- Handle projects with no consumption in the selected range (empty/zero rows
  rather than omitted projects, where the metering data supports it).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a selected time range, per-project GPU-hour consumption reports are
  computed from the metering data delivered by the metering strategy, measured
  by report totals reconciling with the underlying metering data for sampled
  projects and ranges.
- The finalized metering data schema from the GPU usage metering strategy
  (RHAISTRAT-9990) is available and consumed as-is — this epic must not
  re-implement collection or diverge from the delivered schema. (External
  precondition with uncertain timing; this epic is Tier 2 / dependency-gated.)
- Reports are retrievable via a stable API usable by finance tooling, measured
  by a consumer outside the Dashboard retrieving a report successfully.
- Reports are exportable as CSV.
- Report semantics are consistent: what counts as a GPU-hour matches the
  definition agreed for the metering data.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): administrators can view per-project GPU-hour consumption reports
  over selectable time ranges — this epic computes and serves the reports.
- HLR-2 (P1): reports exportable as CSV and retrievable via a stable API for
  finance tooling — this epic delivers the API and export.

# Dashboard admin view for per-project GPU consumption and quota comparison

## Description

This epic delivers the administrator-facing Dashboard view for GPU chargeback
reporting: per-project GPU-hour consumption reports over selectable time
ranges, plus a current-month view showing each project's consumption against
its Kueue quota. It is the console surface on top of the chargeback reporting
capability and the per-project Kueue quota data.

## Scope

- Admin-facing view listing per-project GPU-hour consumption for a selectable
  time range, served from the chargeback reporting capability.
- Current-month view showing each project's consumption against its Kueue
  quota (quota data exposed by the Distributed Workloads side).
- Admin-only visibility (platform administrators, not project users).
- No report computation or metering consumption in this epic — the view
  renders what the reporting capability serves.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given an administrator selects a time range, the view shows per-project
  GPU-hour consumption for that range.
- The current-month view shows each project's consumption against its Kueue
  quota, using the exposed per-project quota data.
- The view is restricted to platform administrators.
- Empty/zero-consumption projects render sensibly in the comparison view.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): administrators can view per-project GPU-hour consumption reports
  over selectable time ranges — this epic delivers the viewing experience.
- HLR-3 (P1): Dashboard admin view shows current-month consumption against
  each project's Kueue quota — this epic renders the comparison.
